A context window is the maximum amount of text, measured in tokens, that a language model can read and consider at one time. It holds everything the model sees: the system prompt, your messages, earlier replies, attached documents, tool results, and the answer it is writing.

The model has no memory outside this window. It only "remembers" what is currently inside it. When a conversation exceeds the limit, the oldest content must be dropped, summarized, or retrieved again later.

Larger windows let the model handle long documents or codebases in one pass. Cost and latency grow with window size. Models can also attend less reliably to details buried in the middle of very long inputs.
